summary: The past 24 hours reveal an AI landscape defined not by consolidation but by a ferocious proliferation of open-weight models and the infrastructure to run them. Ollama's v0.32.5 release — adding Kimi-K2.6, GLM-5.2, MiniMax, DeepSeek, gpt-oss, Qwen, and Gemma in a single drop — crystallizes what Interconnects' latest analysis argues: contrary to predictions of winner-take-all dynamics, labs from Thinking Machines to Xiaomi are investing hundreds of millions to billions in training strong models and releasing them openly, driven by surging token demand. This model abundance is forcing the inference layer to mature rapidly; vLLM's v0.26.0 and a new topology-aware data movement paper exposing 72x bandwidth variation in disaggregated KV cache transfer signal that serving infrastructure is becoming the true competitive frontier. Simultaneously, the agentic stack is hardening — OpenHands v1.8.0 and Dify 1.16.1 demonstrate production-grade AI-driven development and workflow orchestration — while a cluster of papers on LLM-as-judge reliability (Chain-of-Models, the Formalism Trap, ThinkReset) exposes a deepening evaluation crisis: as models judge models, structural biases and consensus mimicry threaten to corrupt the feedback loops that drive improvement. The strategic implication is clear: the moat has shifted from model access to evaluation rigor, serving efficiency, and the ability to compose heterogeneous open models into reliable autonomous systems.

topDevelopments.title: Ollama v0.32.5 Unifies Leading Open Models Into Single Runtime
topDevelopments.summary: Ollama's latest release adds native support for Kimi-K2.6, GLM-5.2, MiniMax, DeepSeek, gpt-oss, Qwen, and Gemma — effectively making the world's most competitive open-weight models locally runnable with a single command. At 177k GitHub stars, Ollama has become the de facto package manager for the open model ecosystem.
topDevelopments.whyItMatters: This release eliminates integration friction across the open model frontier, letting developers swap SOTA models as easily as npm packages and accelerating the shift from API dependence to local sovereignty.
topDevelopments.expectedImpact: Expect rapid proliferation of hybrid model routing in production — using Qwen for coding, Kimi for long-context, DeepSeek for reasoning — with Ollama as the universal substrate.

topDevelopments.title: Interconnects: Open Model Proliferation Defies Consolidation Thesis
topDevelopments.summary: Nathan Lambert's analysis documents a counter-intuitive trend: more companies (Thinking Machines, Xiaomi, and others) are investing hundreds of millions to billions in training strong models and releasing them openly, driven by surging token demand. Thinking Machines, launched February 2025, already generates hundreds of millions in revenue from open-model finetuning.
topDevelopments.whyItMatters: This refutes the prevailing narrative that open models would commoditize into irrelevance; instead, open weights are becoming a viable business model and innovation engine, particularly for non-US labs.
topDevelopments.expectedImpact: Strategic planning must assume a multi-polar open model landscape where competitive advantage comes from finetuning, evaluation, and serving — not base model access.

topDevelopments.title: Topology-Aware Data Movement Exposes 72x Bandwidth Variance in Disaggregated Inference
topDevelopments.summary: A new paper identifies that transferring 2.6 GB KV caches per request for 70B models exceeds 100 GB/s aggregate bandwidth, yet existing systems use uniform RDMA ignoring 72x bandwidth variation across GPU topologies. The proposed topology-aware cache transfer is essential for scalable disaggregated serving.
topDevelopments.whyItMatters: As models grow and disaggregated architectures (prefill/decode separation) become standard, naive data movement will become the primary bottleneck — this work provides the architectural blueprint for the next generation of inference engines like vLLM.
topDevelopments.expectedImpact: Expect vLLM v0.26.0+ and similar engines to integrate topology-aware scheduling as a default, making disaggregated serving viable at scale for the first time.

topDevelopments.title: LLM-as-Judge Evaluation Crisis Deepens Across Multiple Papers
topDevelopments.summary: Three concurrent papers expose systemic flaws: Chain-of-Models reveals cross-model auditing is needed for bias-robust judging; the Formalism Trap introduces the Evaluative Dissonance Index showing judges conflate structural compliance with correctness under social load; ThinkReset demonstrates that long-horizon reasoning accumulates redundancy and error without learnable intermediate interfaces.
topDevelopments.whyItMatters: As the field increasingly relies on LLM judges for RLHF, benchmarking, and automated evaluation, these structural biases risk corrupting the very feedback loops that drive model improvement — a potential 'evaluation collapse' scenario.
topDevelopments.expectedImpact: New evaluation protocols will require multi-judge ensembles, bias auditing pipelines, and explicit reasoning interfaces — moving beyond single-model scoring toward verifiable judgment chains.

topDevelopments.title: OpenHands v1.8.0 and Dify 1.16.1 Signal Agentic Stack Maturation
topDevelopments.summary: OpenHands (82k stars) reaches v1.8.0 as a production-grade AI-driven development agent, while Dify (151k stars) hits 1.16.1 with agentic workflows, RAG pipelines, and collaborative workspaces deployable on cloud, VPC, or self-hosted. Both integrate deeply with the expanding open model ecosystem via Ollama and vLLM.
topDevelopments.whyItMatters: These aren't demos — they're infrastructure. The convergence of mature agent frameworks, universal model runtimes, and high-throughput serving engines means autonomous software development and complex workflow automation are crossing the chasm from research to deployment.
topDevelopments.expectedImpact: Enterprise adoption will accelerate as compliance (self-hosted), model flexibility (Ollama), and reliability (vLLM) align — watch for 'agentic CI/CD' and automated refactoring to become standard within 12 months.

newsletters.title: Latest open artifacts (#23): Laguna S2.1, Inkling, & Kimi K3 show the utility of open models on the Pareto frontier
newsletters.summary: Consolidation has been one of the paths that many astute observers predicted for the near-future of labs training models. It was labelled as inevitable, as training costs are increasing by orders of magnitude every year. Yet, as someone who in 2024 would’ve predicted consolidation really picking up
newsletters.content:
Consolidation has been one of the paths that many astute observers predicted for the near-future of labs training models. It was labelled as inevitable, as training costs are increasing by orders of magnitude every year. Yet, as someone who in 2024 would’ve predicted consolidation really picking up come 2026 or 2027, where are we? We’re at a place where more companies are training strong models — easily investing hundreds of millions to billions of dollars in the total effort still — and an increasing number of organizations are releasing these models openly.

The demand for tokens is incredibly high, and likely to increase as models get more efficient and unlock more possible use cases. All of these labs we thought would need to consolidate are realizing that building token machines is a likely path to value, and more companies will identify that source of value over time.

The prime example is Thinking Machines — when they announced their company in February 2025, very few people would’ve put them in the bucket of an open models company, myself included. Now their open model finetuning service is making hundreds of millions in revenue per year and they’re releasing the best open-weight models built in the U.S.A. — ahead of the early leaders in NVIDIA with Nemotron and Arcee’s Trilogy.

Share

On the other side of the ecosystem is the sustained pace from the Chinese labs, with newer entrants like Xiaomi still accumulating mindshare in the broader AI economy. Having predicted consolidation for a long time, it now seems like a safer bet is to predict continued adoption, and try to imagine the role that open models play there. How much can revenue-share licenses like Kimi K3 stick? How much market share can open models take? We’re entering the decisive era.

This is one of the most packed recaps of open models we’ve ever had, we’re excited!

Our Picks
•
Inkling by thinkingmachines: The first model from Thinking Machines is a 975B-A41B multimodal MoE that supports text, images, and audio as inputs and produces text as output. While it is not the strongest model among peers (in China) in its size class, it is positioned to be a great base for fine-tuning, e.g., through their commercial offering, Tinker. They also release a smaller version (276B-A12B), which is really competitive for its size.

•
Hy3 by tencent: A 295B-A21B MoE from Tencent. It improves over its predecessor across all metrics. Most notable, however, is the license change: While the previous version (covered in Artifacts 21) used a custom and rather restrictive license, Tencent switched to Apache 2 for this release. The model was also able to proof a 50 year old math problem (with a dedicated harness and Sol as a judge, although it is unclear how important the latter really is).

[]

• •

•
Laguna-S-2.1 by poolside: Poolside quickly rose out of nowhere to become a frequent guest at Artifacts, marking its third appearance in three consecutive months. S2.1 is a newly pre- and post-trained version of the 118B-A8B MoE that fits on a DGX Spark, which brought it a lot of attention. Poolside also adopted the OpenMDW license, which is an Apache 2.0-like free license but has better legal backing for AI models specifically. The company also goes into more detail in its blog, which includes all the evaluation trajectories. This is a lot of transparency for an open model release!

•
DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 by deepseek-ai: Just one day after OpenAI has dropped the prices of their smallest model by 80%, the whale dropped an update to their V4 Flash model, beating Luna at the pareto frontier. The bigger model is not updated yet, so it remains to be seen where it will land in terms of performance. For the initial V4 releases, the Flash version was the star of the show in terms of performance per parameter, while Pro was rather underwhelming.

[]

• •

•
Kimi-K3 by moonshotai: This is the biggest open model release in some time, and we covered it in a separate post and a podcast episode. It was released under a noncommercial license, requiring inference and fine-tuning providers to enter into a commercial agreement. Kevin Xu and Graham Webster argue in a post that these licenses enable potential future government action against US entities doing business with Chinese AI companies:

>
But if a US company needs a contract with Moonshot to provide the inference tokens that Kimi K3 generates, the picture looks different. Some of the policy tools US officials and others have debated as potential levers to restrict Chinese open model use would more clearly apply.

Models

General Purpose
•
LongCat-2.0 by meituan-longcat: The Chinese DoorDash is back again. This time, the company released another big MoE with 1.6T parameters. While the model itself is not the most capable for its size beyond benchmarks, it was trained entirely on Ascend 910s, making it the first non-Huawei, non-toy model trained entirely on Chinese accelerators. Other Chinese chips are mostly used for inference (if at all).

•
Laguna-XS-2.1 by poolside: An update to the small (33B-A3B) MoE from Poolside.

•
Motif-3-Beta by Motif-Technologies: A preview of a 314B-A13B MoE by the Korean Motif. This is by far the company’s most ambitious model, as it is considerably larger and introduces some architectural innovations like GDLA and mHC.

•
Apertus-v1.5-70B by swiss-ai: A continued pre-train of the fully open-source Apertus 1.0, using 2T more tokens.

•
Instella-MoE-16B-A3B-Think by amd: A 16B-A3B MoE trained by AMD on Instinct cards. AMD also provides all the different stages, from the base to the SFT checkpoints, as well as MidTrain and DPO.
